events.title: Niklaus Wirth designs Pascal
events.summary: Niklaus Wirth designed Pascal between 1968 and 1970 as a teaching language emphasizing structured programming and clarity — distinct from the November 1970 language report.
events.about: Pascal trained generations through Turbo Pascal and Delphi before yielding to C++ and Java. Wirth also created Modula-2 and Oberon — advocating simplicity with his quote 'Pascal is my favorite language after Pascal.'

narrative.whyChosen: Pascal was the default intro language for a decade of CS education.
narrative.whyImportant: It spread structured programming discipline to millions of students.
narrative.problemSolved: FORTRAN and BASIC taught bad habits; Wirth wanted a small, clear teaching language.

sources.title: ETH Zurich — Wirth, The Programming Language Pascal (1970)
